ShortDescription.Value: Build a ski resort: drawn chairlifts, gondolas and an aerial tram, runs on the game's own snow, lodges and a resort economy. No mods required.

Publish.LongDescription:
**Build a ski resort in Cities: Skylines II.**
Draw chairlifts, gondolas and an aerial tram up your mountain, draw runs down it, and let the game's own snow decide when they open. Guests ski, buy tickets and lessons, and the resort draws tourists to your city. No mods required, but Anarchy and Move It are highly recommended.
## Highlights - **Four lifts, one tool.** Fixed-grip triple chairlift, detachable quad chairlift, gondola and aerial tram. Click the base station, click the top, and the tool plans numbered towers over your terrain. Chairs and cabins ride the rope. - **Runs on real snow.** Draw a run and set its features: groomed or natural, snow guns, floodlights for night skiing. Cat tracks link runs across the hill. Each run is rated green to double black from its hardest pitch. It opens at 3 ft (91 cm) of snow on 60 % of the run. Snow guns extend the season where it is cold enough. - **Resort Planner (experimental).** Outline a mountainside and get a plan of linked runs, cat tracks and lifts. Leave out what you do not want, then build it. - **Seasons.** Snow melts in spring, runs close and lifts stop. The aerial tram keeps running as summer sightseeing. - **Lodges, Ski School and Ski Patrol.** Five lodges, a school and two patrol buildings, each following a real place. - **Merge your own buildings.** A landmark, signature or recreation building near the runs can join a ski area as a lodge and keep working as before. - **Ski Bus Depot.** A coach stop in town that brings guests to a hill too far away to draw them on its own. - **One hub.** The Ski Resort button (top left) opens Attraction, Runs, Lifts, Guests, Finances and History views. It also has a problem list that flies you to what is wrong. - **A resort economy.** Lift tickets, season passes, lessons, lodge spend and running costs. A ski area's attraction score feeds the game's tourism, so a bigger resort brings more visitors.
## Requirements Cities: Skylines II 1.6 (tested on 1.6.4f1). No other mod and no DLC.
## Getting started 1. Open the Ski Resort hub. Place a Welcome Sign snapped to a road (it stands set back from it). Then place a lodge near where the runs will be. 2. Pick a lift type. Place the base station, then the top station facing it, then draw the line between them. Press Enter to build. 3. Connect a low-voltage power line to the base station. 4. Draw runs downhill from the top station, and wait for snow.
## Good to know - Skiers are counted, not simulated. Chairs and cabins move but carry no riders. - Most chairlift and gondola stations cut a level pad into the slope and fill nothing. The fixed-grip top station and the aerial tram's top terminal keep the slope as placed. - Chairlifts and gondolas stop in summer when no run is open. The aerial tram keeps running as sightseeing. - Bulldozing a Welcome Sign also deletes every run linked to it, with the runs' glade trees, and refunds no run fee. A warning shows the run count and asks first. To move a sign, use Relocate in its info panel: its runs stay linked. - The Resort Planner is experimental and off by default: turn it on in Options. Build makes its cat tracks and runs, and Build lifts then adds its lifts one at a time. A lift line the planner cannot fit gets its stations only, and the lift tool opens on it for you to place the towers. On steep ground it plans mostly black runs with few greens. It does not avoid roads or buildings inside the outline. Its Undo covers runs only and ends when the lift build starts. - Lifts cross lifts of another type, over or under, where the towers can reach the height. Two lifts of the same type cannot cross. - A cat track cannot pass under a lift that is already built: build cat tracks first. - Lifts are power-line networks and need low-voltage power at the base station. The game refuses a city high-voltage line at a lift. - Before uninstalling, bulldoze your lifts and runs (or use the Delete all ski resort content button in the mod's Options), then save the city. Otherwise the city still loads, but buildings and stations turn into placeholder blocks and runs stay as flat patches. - Resorts cost money all year and earn in winter. Build in steps.
## Guides and details Guides, every number, settings and troubleshooting are on the docs site: {{DOCS_URL}} Start with the Resort Quickstart at {{DOCS_URL}}/quickstart/ and the Lifts guide at {{DOCS_URL}}/guides/lifts/. Bug reports: the Paradox forum thread {{FORUM_URL}} or the Discord thread {{DISCORD_URL}}. Paste the text from the Copy diagnostics button in the mod's Options. Source code: {{GITHUB_URL}}
## Works with Nothing else is required, but Anarchy and Move It are highly recommended: Anarchy turns off the game's placement errors, and Move It gives exact placement of every building and station. Write Everywhere is recommended too: with it, the Welcome Sign shows your ski area's name (without it, the name board stays plain). If Tourism Overhaul, Realistic Workplaces and Households or a trip-planner mod is installed, the hub shows a notice and changes nothing in them. Realistic Trips replaces the game's leisure system that ski days need: with it, the resort sends no skiers of its own. Lifts, runs, snow and buildings still work.
## Credits - Modular Golf Course Pack by joergeske: the modular recreation idea this mod grew from. - Meapy's Tourism Overhaul: studied for how tourism and attractions work. Not required. - The fixed-grip lift is a tribute to the Pallavicini lift at Arapahoe Basin. - Built with Claude (Anthropic) for decompilation, prefab work and asset generation. Direction and testing by the author. - Full credits and licenses: {{DOCS_URL}}/credits/
**License**: code MIT. Art assets (meshes, textures): CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0/). Reuse them in free mods with credit to "Modular Ski Resort by theotherwildcathighboy", share your changes under the same license, no commercial use.

- Save compatible with previous: n/a (first release) - Layout versions: Binding 1, TreeMember 2, SeasonPass 1, HistoryMonth 2, MonthInProgress 2, RunPropMember 1, RunPropSettings 1, LodgeNumber 1, TrackSnow 1, RunName 1, MergedLodge 1 - Do not load in older versions: no
First public release.
- Four lift types: fixed-grip triple chairlift, detachable quad chairlift, gondola and aerial tram. Chairs and cabins move along the cable, lean downwind and rock in the gusts; the tram shuttles two cabins. A built lift line fells the trees in its corridor. - One lift tool: click the base station and the top station, click the line to add a tower, drag to move one, Enter builds. The tower planner fits tower heights to the terrain with few towers, prefers short towers next to the stations, and draws spans that are too steep in red. Towers are numbered. - Detachable quad and gondola stations and the fixed-grip base station cut a level pad into the slope and fill nothing. A base station cuts 12 m further on the line side, so the chairs leave it over level ground. The aerial tram's base terminal levels its pad. The fixed-grip top station and the aerial tram's top terminal keep the slope. - Ski runs you draw: natural, groomed, snowmaking, night and cat track, each rated green to double black from its slope. - Cat track tool: lay out a track, and one key grades the ground under 25 percent and builds the cat track on it. Where it crosses a run it grades up to 2 m inside the run and keeps the run's difficulty. Delete mode (Ctrl+Shift+D) and a hub trash button remove a track; right click and Esc never do. - Resort Planner (experimental): outline a slope of up to 9 km2. The planner lays out the linked runs and cat tracks first, then proposes the lifts that serve them, each with its way home (green, blue, black only, or ride the lift down). Run colors come from the mod's own run rater. It plans around water, other ski areas, land the city does not own, your existing runs, and existing lifts (stations and a 10 m corridor along the line). It does not avoid roads or buildings. Leave out runs or lifts and set how many runs and the run features. Build makes the cat tracks and then the runs in one go, and Undo removes that build and refunds it. Build lifts then adds the kept lifts one at a time, lowest first. A line whose towers fit builds; a line with one tower up to 5 degrees over its limit builds and its row says which tower; a line the planner cannot fit gets its stations, the other lifts still build, and the lift tool then opens on it. The scan runs in the background with a progress line, and right click stops it. Optional tree filler. Ctrl+Shift+Q; it is off by default and is turned on in Options. - Safety Net Fence: decorative orange netting on thin poles, in the hub's Runs tab. - Snow-depth run system: runs open at 3 ft (91 cm) on 60 percent of the run and stay open while 1 ft covers 40 percent, snow guns on snowmaking and night runs (two months before winter to one month after), powder days, seasons. - Snow guns, hydrants and floodlights stand at a set distance along a run's edge, however its outline was drawn, with two values per run in the Runs view. Cat tracks carry guns and hydrants on one side, and pay snowmaking upkeep by plan area while their guns can run; with the gun value at Off, none, and snow already made stays until it melts. - Welcome Sign (set back 8 m from the road on a leveled lot), five lodges, Ski School, two patrol buildings. - The Welcome Sign is the ski area: runs, lifts and buildings within its radius belong to it (5 km by default, 2 to 10 km in Options). While placing a sign, a ring shows the radius and the tooltip gives the height under the cursor, the lowest and highest dry ground in the ring, the vertical above the winter snow line, and how much ground lies above it. A selected sign shows its ring too. - Lodge parking: car spaces within 600 m of a lodge with a road count for it (street parking, parking lots, a parking garage at its entrance); tourist parties drive in and need them. A blue ring shows the 600 m while placing or selecting a lodge. - Ski Bus Depot: a coach stop in town for the nearest ski area, at any distance. A home closer to it than to a lodge starts its ski day there; guests pay as at a lodge. It adds no skier room and no score, needs a hill lodge, and bills 1,500 a month plus 300 per km to that lodge (Finances, row Ski bus). An oxblood coach, with SKI BUS painted on it, drives between the depot and the hill. Selecting the coach or the depot shows a Ski Bus card beside the game's panel: guests by bus this month, the coach bill and the distance to the hill lodge. - Merge an existing building into a ski area as a lodge: a park, landmark, signature or decor building near the runs can be merged as a lodge tier its lot allows. It keeps working as before and adds score, skier room, staff and attraction, for a one-time charge and a monthly fee. The Mergeable buildings switch on the hub's Buildings tab (and in the Attraction view's Merged buildings fold) outlines the buildings near the runs and lifts that can be merged, green when a lodge tier fits the lot and gray when the lot is too small; the merge card beside the info panel says whether a building is near enough to count before you pay. - The Ski Resort panel: Attraction, Runs, Lifts, Guests, Finances and History views, a problem list and a build strip. - Economy: lift tickets, season passes, lessons, lodge spend, off-season half staff. - Delete all ski resort content, a button in the mod's Options (Reset group): removes everything the mod placed in the loaded city, after a confirmation, to clean a city before uninstalling. It cannot be undone. - Copy diagnostics, a button in the mod's Options (Diagnostics group): puts the versions, the changed options, the code mods and the latest log errors on the clipboard for a bug report. - Works on the base game; no other mod is required. Write Everywhere is recommended, and Move It is useful for exact placement. - Known limitations: the Resort Planner's Undo ends when the tool closes, a scan of a large outline can take about 30 seconds, a hill far from the city's homes and hotels gets few ski-day guests (the panel shows the distance), chairs carry no riders, two lifts of the same type cannot cross, a cat track cannot pass under a lift that is already built, the fixed-grip top station and the aerial tram's top terminal keep the slope and can sit partly in the hillside on steep ground, chairlifts and gondolas stop in summer.
